correctness.rationale: PASS: With u=2b+1, u satisfies u_{n+2}=6u_{n+1}-u_n. Squaring produces roots 1,alpha,alpha^-1,alpha^2,alpha^-2; the constant contribution is 5/16. R(T)=(T^2-6T+1)(T^2-34T+1), R(1)=128, yields R(T)b_n^2=40. Summing across each window gives a *monic* inhomogeneous fourth-order recurrence R(T)H_k(n)=40k, so gcd of all windows equals gcd(40k, first four). Residues b_n mod 3 and 5 have periods 4 and 6 and imply every 12-block of squares divisible by 15. Mod-4 periodicity gives H_4(n)=8 mod16. Matrix M=[[6,-1,2],[1,0,0],[0,0,1]] and 2-adic squaring prove M^{2^m}=I+2^mC mod2^{m+1} for m>=2 and therefore H_{2^m}(n)=2^{m+1} mod 2^{m+2} for all n,m. Three successive dyadic blocks give exact v2(H_{12*2^r})=r+3, combined with odd factor 15 and the 40k upper divisor yields exact G(k)=120*2^r. Independent exact recurrence checks at 400 indices; gcd first-four versus 100 windows for every k=1..119 and six dyadic lengths; all pass. Finite testing is not the proof of infinite lifting.

The recurrence-gcd method is classical; original scope is the 40k universal reduction and exact infinite dyadic family. An unindexed later solution of Question 30 remains possible.
